title: Exact 1/3 tolerance with geometric filtering, square-root exponential work and linear quantum space

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, set n = ceil(log2 N). The geometric-filter algorithm with exactly the single parameter rule and complete schedule of proof.md Section 0, under every adversary of the fifth claim, including the clean problem, outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 11/16 > 2/3. All four resource bounds hold simultaneously on every execution branch, including all failures, with absolute constants independent of N, s, supplier and outcomes. Total work counts source acquisition, all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, addresses, preparation, measurements, resets, initialization and every capped attempt; memory includes all retained workspace. The SAME algorithm/configuration has total sequential work T = O(2^{n/2} n^5 (log2 n)^2), with exact representative-envelope growth index 1. See proof.md Sections 0-9.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, set n = ceil(log2 N). The geometric-filter algorithm with exactly the single parameter rule and complete schedule of proof.md Section 0, under every adversary of the fifth claim, including the clean problem, outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 11/16 > 2/3. All four resource bounds hold simultaneously on every execution branch, including all failures, with absolute constants independent of N, s, supplier and outcomes. Total work counts source acquisition, all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, addresses, preparation, measurements, resets, initialization and every capped attempt; memory includes all retained workspace. The proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=1/3 for every N >= 2 with no threshold. At most floor(Q/3)=Q/3 acquired copies are malformed on every branch. Their positions and arbitrary states may be adaptive with all earlier actual measurement outcomes and a private quantum system; malformed copies may be mutually entangled. Every clean delivery is a fresh independent ideal state in tensor product with everything else. The supplier has no post-delivery access to algorithm systems. This holds jointly with all four declared bounds for this SAME algorithm/configuration. The byte-exact model is stated in proof.md Section 0, and Sections 1-9 prove the complete guarantee.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
